finding: 50,000 loans, $797M originated Jan 2021 - Dec 2024, average rate 16.6%
8.8% of loans issued 2021-2023 defaulted within 24 months
the grade ranks risk: 2.8% (A) to 26.8% (G) default within 24 months, 9.5x
the 2023 vintage reached 10.1% defaults by month 24 vs 7.1% for 2021: it met the 2024 unemployment rise early in life
online loans with DTI 40-50% (allowed from Jul 2023) default at 6.4% in 12 months vs 3.8% for the rest (1.7x); they pay 5.3 pts more interest, more than the ~1.9 pts a year of extra expected loss
loss given default 72.3%: 66.3% for homeowners with a mortgage vs 77.4% for renters
the scorecard's Gini on 2023 loans (out of time) is 0.38 vs 0.32 for the lender's grade
the worst score band defaults 9.7x as often as the best
all 15 estimated risk effects have the true sign (correlation with the truth 0.97)
each +1 pt of unemployment raises monthly default starts by 35% (true: 35%)
IFRS 9 ECL at 31 Dec 2025: $6.48M on a $172.6M open book (3.76% coverage)
backtest: at Dec 2024 the model expected 1,525 defaults in 2025 (scenario-weighted); 1,290 happened. With 2025's actual unemployment it would have said 1,371
